reason: Reproduced exactly, through the real interaction path (owner-flight, click a row's Edit control), not just the fixture state. render-b.js openEditor() writes --b-sheet once, guarded on getComputedStyle(node).position === 'fixed'; closeEditor removes it; nothing else ever writes it. render-core.js binds resize -> settle(), and __TLD.b.settle (render-b.js:1738) only re-places .b-measure nodes, so the reserve is never recomputed. Measured with Playwright/chromium on master.html?v=approach: open the editor at 1440x960 (panel position:relative in the rail) and resize to 768x1024 -> panel flips to position:fixed, --b-sheet still (unset), .b-field padding-bottom 28px (var(--gap-block)) and scroll-padding-bottom 30px, document height 2499px. The identical editor opened natively at 768x1024 -> --b-sheet 583px, padding-bottom 583px, scroll-padding-bottom 583px, document 3054px. 555px of reserved layout missing, exactly as the finding states. Scrolled to true max scroll (atMaxScroll true) two row 'Edit' controls sit inside the sheet's rect with no scroll left to free them; natively opened at 768 the same test strands zero. At 390 after the same resize: one stranded, native 390 zero. The iPad case is the one that makes this a real person's path rather than a synthetic resize: open at 1194x834 (landscape, >=1024, rail) and rotate to 834x1194 (portrait, sheet) -> --b-sheet (unset), padding 28px, two Edit controls covered at max scroll; opened natively at 834x1194 the reserve is 583px and zero are covered. A laptop window dragged in past 1024 with the editor open does the same. Not already handled, and not a restatement of the gate: interaction-check.mjs:1001 ('the sheet reserves its own band @ 390/768') and its stranded-controls companion only ever run on a page LOADED at that width via open({viewport}), never on one resized into it, so the whole resize path is unwalked. This is the paid-for lessons.md class 'Floating objects erase what is under them' (lessons.md:83) returning through that path. Verified the proposed fix by simulating reserve() on resize in the live page: at 768 -> 583px / doc 3054 / 0 covered, at 390 -> 583px / 0 covered, at 834 -> 583px / 0 covered, back at 1440 -> var removed, padding 56px, doc 2130, identical to native 1440. It converges and is idempotent in both directions. Note the reverse direction is currently benign but leaves state dirty: open at 768 (--b-sheet 583px) and widen to 1440 and the variable stays set at 583px; a heavier min-width:1024 rule wins so computed padding is still 56px, but the removeProperty branch of the fix cleans that latent staleness up too. Real, specific, cheap, and below a 9.5 bar as it stands.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed, with two sharpenings. (1) Do not resolve root inside settle as document.querySelector('.b-field[data-editor-open]') - measured, the [data-editor-open] attribute is set on the .b-field root by openEditor, so document.querySelector('[data-editor-open]') is the honest selector and survives the attribute moving; then reserve(root) reads root.querySelector('.b-edit') and returns silently when there is none, so the helper is a no-op on the twelve states with no editor open. (2) Keep the else branch as removeProperty, not a write of 0 - that is what makes the widen direction converge back to the native 1440 values (var unset, padding 56px, document 2130px) instead of leaving a stale 583px that a future CSS change could start honouring. Call it from openEditor() in place of the one-shot write and from __TLD.b.settle, which render-core.js already runs on the rAF-debounced resize and on fonts.ready, so no new listener is added and no new measurement pass is introduced. For the gate, extend the existing 390/768 loop rather than adding a third block: after the current native assertions, resize the page to the other width (768 -> 390 and, in a second page, open at 1440 then setViewportSize 768 and 390), scroll to document.documentElement.scrollHeight, and assert both that .b-field padding-bottom >= panel.offsetHeight and that zero .b-grab rects intersect the panel rect - the intersection test must include the horizontal axis (r.right > panel.left && r.left < panel.right), because at desk width the rail panel and the measure column overlap vertically without ever covering anything, and a vertical-only test reports two false strandings at 1440.
